text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti says all levels of Jordanian society appreciate Kuwait's decision to release 10 Jordanian prisoners and hope this will lead to further releases and a return to political relations with the the Gulf emirate.
- Crown Prince Hassan says fulfilling the rights of Moslems, Christians and Jews in Jerusalem is a basis for achieving peace.
- Finance Minister Marwan Awad says import duty on cars will be slashed from Sunday to 40 percent -- sales tax will be increased to make up the difference.

- Efforts to constrain the threat of a new Iraqi-Jordanian crisis centred around three issues: Iraq's refusal to hand over its report into investigation of Jordanian embassy driver's murder; sentencing of two Jordanians to death for possessing illegal matter; and Jordan's request for information on Jordanians detained in Iraq.
- Information Minister Marwan Muasher says the rights of Jordanian refugees of Palestinian origin are Jordan's responsibility.
- U.S. ambassador Wesley Egan says United States has a strong interest in stability of Jordan and alliance with it.
- Prince Hassan not to visit Israel on Saturday, will only go when visit serves the cause of peace. Crown Prince's decision not to go is a strong message of protest.
